label: Write
summary: Turn speech into clean text for the field focused when you choose Stop, with a saved recovery path when delivery is blocked.
proof: Local transcription is the default; optional shaping is a separate decision.

opening.title: Speak once. Stop at the field where your words belong.
opening.summary: Use Mumble’s deliberate Dictate command and speak while the Island shows what is happening. Keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop. When Stop is requested, Mumble freezes that field as the destination. It then attempts one delivery.

demonstration.title: See where your words return.
demonstration.spoken: Move the design review to Thursday and send the notes before lunch.
demonstration.note: Illustrative cursor close-up—not a live transcription. The Mumble workspace above is a genuine product capture.

states.label: Choose cursor
states.title: Keep the intended field ready for Stop.
states.body: Place the cursor in the writing field where you want the finished text. Keep it focused, or return to it, before choosing Stop.

states.label: Speak
states.title: Mumble makes its state visible.
states.body: Use the global Dictate command and speak. Before choosing Stop, keep or return focus to the intended field. The Island shows Listening, then Transcribing.

states.label: Text returned
states.title: Stop freezes the intended destination.
states.body: When Stop is requested, Mumble freezes the focused field for one target-bound insertion. If delivery cannot complete, the result remains recoverable in the Deck.
states.field: Project note — Move the design review to Thursday and send the notes before lunch.

mechanism.title: One deliberate command. One visible route back.
mechanism.summary: Write keeps the Stop-time destination, processing state, privacy route, delivery attempt, and recovery path in one understandable sequence.

steps.title: Keep the intended field focused for Stop
steps.body: Place the cursor in a writable field. Keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop. Mumble then uses the field focused at Stop instead of asking you to move into a separate editor.
steps.proof: The destination is frozen when Stop is requested—not when recording starts.

steps.title: Start with the deliberate global Dictate command
steps.body: Invoke Dictate from the application you are already using. The Island shows Listening, then Transcribing, so recording and processing are visible rather than implied.
steps.proof: The same global command starts and stops the dictation.

steps.title: Transcribe on this computer by default
steps.body: Local transcription is the default. Recorded audio stays on this computer unless the user explicitly selects Cloud transcription.
steps.proof: Optional shaping is a separate finished-text decision.

steps.title: Return once, or recover safely
steps.body: Mumble attempts to insert the finished text at the field frozen when Stop was requested. If insertion cannot complete, the result is saved in the Deck and History for Copy or Paste latest instead of being sent again automatically.
steps.proof: Later focus changes do not authorize a new destination or a second blind insertion.

tasks.title: Everyday notes
tasks.summary: Add a complete thought to the note already open in front of you.
steps: Place the cursor at the point where the note should continue.
Use the global Dictate command and speak the thought in ordinary language.
Keep or return focus to that field before you choose Stop; the Island then shows the transition into transcription.
Continue from the inserted text, or use the saved Deck result if delivery could not complete.

tasks.title: Longer text
tasks.summary: Draft a connected passage without replacing the document you already chose.
steps: Place the cursor in the draft where the next passage belongs.
Start Dictate and speak the passage at a comfortable pace.
Keep or return focus to that field before you choose Stop; the Island then shows the transition into transcription.
Review the returned text in the draft, or recover the finished result from the Deck if insertion was blocked.

tasks.title: Across applications
tasks.summary: Carry the same Write sequence into another writable desktop application.
steps: Open the destination application and place its cursor in the intended field.
Invoke the global Dictate command without leaving that application.
Speak, then keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop.
Mumble attempts one return to the field frozen at Stop; if that field is unavailable at delivery, it keeps the text in the Deck rather than inserting elsewhere.

label: Capture
summary: Record microphone meetings into a local, searchable working record you can review and export.
proof: Mumble saves the recording locally before transcription and later analysis.

label: Shape
summary: Give finished text a deliberate job: Prompt, Email, Reply, language assistance, presets, custom shaping, or analysis.
proof: Cloud text shaping is optional and sends finished text—not recorded audio—through the chosen route.

opening.title: Start local. Shape only when the words need another job.
opening.summary: Mumble’s default Text path already returns useful, punctuated dictation. Shape is an optional next layer for a prompt, email, reply, language-assisted text, or a chosen analysis preset.

demonstration.title: See one finished thought become a structured prompt.
demonstration.spoken: Plan a design review for Thursday. Ask for the three highest-risk usability issues, evidence for each, and the next action.
demonstration.note: Illustrative Shape demonstration—not a live provider result. It shows the product’s real Prompt mode and privacy boundary without claiming a provider outcome.

states.label: Finished text
states.title: Begin with text that is already useful.
states.body: Default Text cleanup is deterministic and local. It needs no Mumble account, provider key, or paid service.
states.field: Plan a design review for Thursday. Ask for the three highest-risk usability issues, evidence for each, and the next action.

states.label: Choose Prompt
states.title: Choose the job before the route runs.
states.body: Prompt is a deliberate mode. If its effective route is hosted, Mumble sends this finished text—not recorded audio—using the configured provider and key. External providers may charge.
states.fieldLabel: Finished text waiting for the chosen route
states.field: Plan a design review for Thursday. Ask for the three highest-risk usability issues, evidence for each, and the next action.

states.label: Shaped prompt
states.title: Review the shaped text before using it.
states.body: This example illustrates the structured form Mumble’s Prompt mode requests. It does not promise a provider’s wording, quality, or speed.
states.field:
Role: Act as a usability reviewer.
Task: Review the design planned for Thursday.
Return: The three highest-risk usability issues, evidence for each, and one next action.

mechanism.title: Shape routes finished text with the choice frozen.
mechanism.summary: The mode, selected material, provider route, model, and privacy boundary are captured for one shaping action. A hosted route cannot silently become another provider or take the recorded audio with it.

steps.title: Keep Text useful without AI
steps.body: Text is the everyday default: deterministic local cleanup produces punctuated text without an account or provider key. Foreign is a separate opt-in local term-assistance mode that prioritises the languages chosen in Settings rather than translating the whole result.
steps.proof: Local dictation remains useful with no Mumble account, provider key, or paid service.

steps.title: Choose Prompt, Email, or Reply deliberately
steps.body: Prompt asks for a structured role, task, constraints, and output. Email requests a greeting, body, sign-off, and an optional subject. Reply uses selected context to draft a direct response. Each is a real shaping form, not a generic chat assistant.
steps.proof: Text, Prompt, Email, Reply, and Foreign remain distinct modes.

steps.title: Apply a preset or custom shaping instruction
steps.body: The Deck offers 20 built-in presets for actions such as Improve, Make shorter, Deep Thinking, Summarise, and Extract facts, plus five custom shaping slots the user can define. A chosen mode can also control the final form.
steps.proof: Analysis is a chosen preset action over selected material—not an automatic claim about every dictation.

steps.title: Freeze the effective configured route
steps.body: Cerebras and OpenRouter are the current supported hosted text choices in Settings. A user-supplied key and a confirmed model are required before the hosted route is ready. External providers may charge under their own terms.
steps.proof: Hosted shaping sends finished text—not recorded audio—and cannot swap to another provider silently.

steps.title: Treat local shaping as configuration-dependent
steps.body: A compatible local model can be used only when the user separately supplies and enables it. No local model is bundled or adopted, so the website does not present local Prompt, Email, or Reply shaping as an out-of-box result.
steps.proof: Device-only remains a fail-closed privacy choice when hosted processing is unavailable or disabled.

steps.title: Review the saved result
steps.body: A completed Deck shaping job is saved before Mumble attempts the selected field. The visitor examples describe the sequence and form only; they do not promise a provider’s exact output, quality, or speed.
steps.proof: Illustrative text is labelled wherever it is not a genuine product capture.

modes.label: Text
modes.summary: Clean, punctuated everyday dictation with deterministic local processing.

modes.label: Prompt
modes.summary: Turns a rough request into a structured role, task, constraints, and expected output.

modes.label: Email
modes.summary: Requests a complete email form with greeting, body, sign-off, and an optional subject.

modes.label: Reply
modes.summary: Drafts a direct response from the selected context and the user’s instruction.

modes.label: Foreign
modes.summary: Prioritises chosen non-English terms locally and preserves them instead of anglicising them.

tasks.title: AI prompt
tasks.summary: Turn one finished thought into a structured prompt without presenting Mumble as an AI chat product.
steps: Dictate the complete request with ordinary Text; default transcription and cleanup stay local.
Choose Prompt so the requested role, task, constraints, and output form are explicit.
Mumble freezes the effective configured route. A hosted route requires the user’s provider key and sends finished text—not recorded audio; external providers may charge.
Review the shaped prompt, then paste or recover the saved result from the Deck. Any example on this site is illustrative, not a provider-output promise.

tasks.title: Business email
tasks.summary: Shape rough finished text into an email form while keeping the route visible.
steps: Dictate the facts, recipient, and purpose in your own words using the useful local Text path.
Choose Email; include an optional recipient or subject only when the finished text supplies one.
Mumble uses the frozen effective route. If hosted, only the finished text leaves through the configured provider and key; external providers may charge.
Review the greeting, body, sign-off, and any subject before using the saved result. The website does not claim a provider’s quality or wording.

tasks.title: Contextual reply
tasks.summary: Use selected material and a spoken instruction to draft a direct response.
steps: Select the relevant saved material in the Deck so the reply context is deliberate rather than ambient.
Choose Reply and state what the response should communicate.
Mumble freezes the selected context, instruction, and effective route for that job. Hosted processing sends that finished text context—not recorded audio—and external providers may charge.
Review the direct reply and its register before Mumble attempts the selected field; recover the saved result if delivery is blocked.

tasks.title: Language-assisted text
tasks.summary: Preserve chosen non-English terms without implying automatic translation.
steps: Choose the relevant Foreign languages in Settings and keep Foreign assistance opt-in.
Dictate normally; transcription stays local by default and the local term booster prioritises the selected languages.
Use the preserved finished text directly with no Mumble account, provider key, or paid service, or deliberately choose a separate shaping action afterward.
Review names and terms before using the text. Foreign assists preservation; this sequence does not promise translation or hosted-language quality.

label: Listen
summary: Read documents with saved progress, find, bookmarks, summaries, and optional voice playback.
proof: Provider-backed speech is an explicit online choice and may carry the provider's own cost.

label: Find
summary: Use Mumble Find to search local apps and files without hosted results entering the list.
proof: Web Search is separate and sends selected text online only after provider-named confirmation.
